verdict.rationale: ObsessionDB's documented ingestion page says INSERT, the Kafka table engine, and materialized views all work as documented. It also recommends async inserts so the server buffers small streaming writes into larger parts, and packed storage cuts object writes per part. Together these cover the core of a documented streaming ingestion path. Missing for 10: any stated ingest-to-query latency proving writes become queryable within seconds, independent or hands-on corroboration of streaming freshness, and detail on async-insert flush behavior on the object-storage layer.
